text: The new server's config doesn't include a `replicaof` line, so it stays a primary after a restart. I'll also save its data to disk now:

The new Redis 8.10 server (port 6380) now has an exact copy of the 7.2 data and is running as a standalone primary that accepts writes.

**How I copied the data:** I made the new server a temporary replica of the current one (`REPLICAOF 127.0.0.1 6379`). A full replication sync copies every database with types, values, TTLs and stream consumer groups intact. The sync finished cleanly: 3,270 keys loaded and both servers at the same replication position. I then ran `REPLICAOF NO ONE` to make the new server a standalone primary again.

**Checks after the switch:**
- **Key counts:** match in both databases that hold data: db0 has 2,920 keys (900 with a TTL) and db2 has 350 keys (150 with a TTL).
- **Types and TTLs:** every key has the same type on both servers, and remaining TTLs differ by no more than 5 seconds. Consumer groups match on all 20 streams.
- **Values:** all string, list, set, sorted set and hash values are identical. For streams, I compared the full stream details: entries, groups, consumers and pending messages are all identical. The only differences are an internal memory-layout counter and some new fields that only Redis 8 reports.
- **Writes:** a test write and delete on the new server worked.

**Current server:** still running on port 6379 as a primary, with no replica attached. Its data wasn't changed; the only effect was the background snapshot the sync takes.

**New server:**
- Its config file has no `replicaof` line, so it will stay a primary after a restart.
- I ran `SAVE` on it, so its data is also on disk in `/var/lib/redis/dump.rdb`.

The current server is still running and can still take writes. Anything written to it from now until the applications are switched won't reach the new server, so switch the applications promptly.
